countries.name: United States
countries.summary: Executive Order on Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy AI (Oct 2023). NIST AI Risk Management Framework. Sector-specific regulations across finance, healthcare, and defense.
frameworks: Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights
countries.authority: White House OSTP, NIST, sector regulators
highlights: Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights (Oct 2022)
Voluntary AI commitments from major companies
expansion_notes: Monitor evolving executive policy — EO 14110 was revoked in Jan 2025
NIST AI RMF provides a stable compliance baseline across sectors
Sector-specific rules vary widely (FDA for health, OCC for finance)
Strong IP protection and established AI talent market

countries.name: European Union
countries.summary: EU AI Act — the world's first comprehensive AI law. Risk-based approach categorizing AI systems into unacceptable, high, limited, and minimal risk tiers.
highlights: Bans on social scoring and real-time biometric surveillance
High-risk AI requirements: conformity assessments, transparency
expansion_notes: Full EU AI Act compliance required by Aug 2026 for high-risk systems
Appoint an EU representative; register in the EU AI database
GDPR data transfer restrictions require SCCs or adequacy decisions
Significant fines possible — up to €35M or 7% of global turnover

countries.name: China
countries.summary: Multiple targeted AI regulations: Generative AI measures, algorithm recommendation rules, deep synthesis rules. National New Generation AI Development Plan.
highlights: National AI Development Plan targeting global leadership by 2030
expansion_notes: Foreign company access highly restricted in AI-sensitive sectors
All personal data must be stored locally; cross-border transfer requires security assessment
Generative AI products require government security review before launch
Consider a local JV structure to navigate regulatory and market requirements

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.summary: Pro-innovation, principles-based approach. Existing sector regulators apply AI oversight. AI Safety Summit hosted at Bletchley Park (Nov 2023).
countries.authority: DSIT, sector regulators (FCA, ICO, CMA, etc.)
highlights: AI Safety Summit at Bletchley Park (Nov 2023)
expansion_notes: Light-touch, principles-based regulation — one of the most AI-friendly jurisdictions
Sector regulators (FCA, ICO, CMA) issue guidance relevant to your industry
Post-Brexit UK-EU adequacy decision covers most data transfer needs
Government actively welcomes AI investment; Innovate UK funding available

countries.name: Canada
countries.summary: Artificial Intelligence and Data Act (AIDA) proposed under Bill C-27. Voluntary code of conduct for generative AI. Pan-Canadian AI Strategy.
highlights: Voluntary Code of Conduct for Generative AI (Sep 2023)
expansion_notes: AIDA (Bill C-27) has stalled — regulatory uncertainty for high-impact AI systems
Voluntary Code of Conduct is current compliance baseline for generative AI
Quebec's Law 25 adds enhanced privacy obligations beyond federal law
Strong talent base through pan-Canadian AI strategy hubs (Montreal, Toronto, Edmonton)

countries.name: Japan
countries.summary: Agile governance approach. AI Strategy 2022. Hiroshima AI Process under G7 presidency. Voluntary guidelines for generative AI.
highlights: Voluntary guidelines for generative AI providers
expansion_notes: Voluntary, agile governance — no binding AI law; favorable for early movers
Government actively pursuing AI industry partnerships via METI
Japanese language and cultural localization investment needed for consumer products
Strong existing frameworks in automotive and industrial/manufacturing AI

countries.name: South Korea
countries.summary: National AI Strategy. AI industry promotion focused legislation. Seoul AI Safety Summit (May 2024) co-hosted with UK.
highlights: AI Industry Promotion Act under development
expansion_notes: AI Industry Promotion Act in development — monitor for binding requirements
PIPA personal data law applies to all AI-processed personal data
Strong digital infrastructure and deep AI talent pool
Government subsidies and R&D tax credits available for tech sector investment

countries.name: Australia
countries.summary: Australia's AI Ethics Framework (voluntary). Safe and Responsible AI consultation. Mandatory guardrails for high-risk AI proposed.
expansion_notes: Mandatory guardrails for high-risk AI under consultation — plan ahead for 2025-26
Existing AI Ethics Principles provide voluntary compliance guidance
Strong rule of law, IP protection, and English-language market
Government's Responsible AI program offers compliance toolkits

countries.name: India
countries.summary: India AI Mission ($1.2B). Advisory on AI deployment. IndiaAI initiative. No binding AI law yet — innovation-first approach.
expansion_notes: India AI Mission offers compute access and government partnership opportunities
Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA) compliance required for personal data
MeitY advisory for AI intermediaries includes content restrictions
Large and growing market — localization and local partnerships strongly recommended

countries.name: Brazil
countries.summary: AI Bill under debate in Congress. Brazilian AI Strategy (EBIA). LGPD (data protection law) applies to AI. Responsible AI principles adopted.
highlights: LGPD applies to AI data processing
expansion_notes: AI Bill (PL 2338/2023) pending — compliance framework will change on enactment
LGPD (data protection) compliance currently required for AI using personal data
Large consumer market with rapidly growing AI adoption, especially in fintech
High-risk AI use cases will face enhanced scrutiny under the proposed bill

countries.name: Singapore
countries.summary: Model AI Governance Framework (2019, updated 2020). AI Verify testing toolkit. National AI Strategy 2.0 (2023). ASEAN AI Governance.
expansion_notes: Most business-friendly AI environment in Southeast Asia
AI Verify testing toolkit provides a practical compliance pathway
PDPA data protection is mature, well-understood, and consistently enforced
Ideal ASEAN hub: use Singapore as base to serve regional markets

countries.name: Germany
countries.summary: Implementing EU AI Act. National AI Strategy. KI-Bundesverband. Coalition agreement emphasizes innovation with guardrails.
highlights: Implementing EU AI Act as EU member
Focus on AI in industrial/manufacturing sectors
expansion_notes: EU AI Act compliance mandatory — Germany has a strict enforcement culture
Strong industrial AI sector with established Mittelstand partnership opportunities
SPRIND (Federal Agency for Disruptive Innovation) offers R&D funding
High regulatory burden offset by large market size and exceptional stability

countries.name: France
countries.summary: Active in EU AI Act negotiations. National AI strategy. Comité de l'IA Générative report. Paris AI Action Summit (Feb 2025).
highlights: CNIL guidance on GDPR and AI
expansion_notes: EU AI Act compliance mandatory; CNIL is actively issuing AI enforcement guidance
Paris AI Action Summit signaled government openness to AI investment
€2.5B national AI strategy creates significant public-sector partnership opportunities
French language localization required for consumer-facing and public-sector AI

countries.name: Israel
countries.summary: Regulatory principles for AI published. National AI Plan. Innovation Authority guidelines. Principles-based approach favoring innovation.
highlights: Focus on AI in defense and health
expansion_notes: Light-touch, innovation-friendly regulatory approach with no binding AI law
Principles-based framework provides flexibility but limited legal certainty
Deep AI talent pool (military tech to commercial); strong R&D ecosystem
Geopolitical risk requires separate risk assessment for partnerships and supply chain

countries.name: South Africa
countries.summary: National AI Policy Framework (2022). POPIA applies to AI. Presidential Commission on the Fourth Industrial Revolution.
expansion_notes: POPIA compliance required; National AI Policy Framework is voluntary
Presidential 4IR Commission signals positive government attitude toward AI
Growing fintech and healthcare AI market with English-language business environment
Infrastructure gaps may limit deployment scale — assess connectivity requirements

countries.name: UAE
countries.summary: National AI Strategy 2031. Ministry of AI established. AI University. UAE AI regulatory principles. Proactive adoption approach.
highlights: Mohamed bin Zayed University of AI
expansion_notes: Ministry of AI provides dedicated government support for AI companies
Dubai and Abu Dhabi free zones offer IP-friendly structures and tax benefits
Personal Data Protection Law is relatively new — ensure full compliance
Strong government appetite for AI partnerships; public sector is a key buyer

countries.name: Mexico
countries.summary: No AI-specific law. Data protection law (LFPDPPP) applies. National Digital Strategy. Legislative discussions on AI ethics.
highlights: LFPDPPP data protection applies to AI
expansion_notes: No AI-specific law — operate under LFPDPPP and sector-specific regulations
USMCA membership facilitates cross-border data flows with the US and Canada
Growing domestic AI ecosystem, especially in fintech and e-commerce
Monitor political environment closely — policy direction has shifted significantly

countries.name: Nigeria
countries.summary: National AI Strategy (2022). NDPR data protection applies. AI Ethics Framework. Focus on AI for development goals.
highlights: Focus on fintech and agriculture AI
expansion_notes: Early-stage AI regulation — first-mover advantage possible in key sectors
NDPR compliance required as baseline data protection obligation
Fintech and agriculture AI are the strongest growth sectors for early entry
Infrastructure and power reliability challenges must be factored into deployment planning

countries.name: Kenya
countries.summary: Draft AI policy under development. Data Protection Act (2019) applies. iHub tech ecosystem. Focus on fintech AI applications.
countries.authority: ICT Authority, Office of Data Protection Commissioner
highlights: Silicon Savannah hub for AI innovation
expansion_notes: Data Protection Act (2019) in force — ODPC compliance required
AI policy still in draft — early engagement with the ICT Authority is advisable
Silicon Savannah ecosystem provides strong local partnerships and talent
Fintech AI is particularly well-suited: M-Pesa infrastructure widely adopted

countries.name: Russia
countries.summary: National AI Development Strategy to 2030. Federal AI project. Regulatory sandboxes. Sovereign approach to AI with state direction.
expansion_notes: Significant geopolitical and sanctions risk for international companies
Strict data localization law — all personal data must be stored on Russian servers
State-directed AI development limits foreign company operational independence
Not recommended for most international AI expansion due to sanctions environment

advanced.label: Advanced
advanced.description: Comprehensive legislation or frameworks in place or near adoption

developing.label: Developing
developing.description: Active policy development with partial frameworks or voluntary guidelines

emerging.label: Emerging
emerging.description: Early-stage policies or strategy documents; limited binding regulation

minimal.label: Minimal / None
minimal.description: No significant AI-specific policy activity identified
